title: The Town That Said No to Plastic Bags
intro: You are going to read about a small English town that stopped using plastic bags.

passage: Modbury is a quiet little town in the south-west of England. About 1,500 people live there, and it has one main street with a few small shops. But in 2007, newspapers and TV programmes all over the world talked about it. Why? Because Modbury became the first town in Europe without plastic bags.

The idea came from Rebecca Hosking, a local woman who made films about wildlife. In 2006, she was working on some islands near Hawaii, in the Pacific Ocean. There, she saw terrible things. Sea birds and turtles were dying because they ate pieces of plastic. The water looked clean and blue, but there was rubbish everywhere. Plastic in the sea harms millions of animals every year. Rebecca came home sad and angry.

Rebecca wanted to protect the sea, but she knew one person could not change the world. So she started with her own town. She invited all the shop owners to watch her film. After that, she did not need long to persuade them. Every shop agreed to stop giving plastic bags to customers. Instead, they sold cheap reusable bags made of cotton, and some shops used paper bags.

At first, some people forgot their bags at home, and shopping was not easy. But slowly it became a habit. Older people said it was like the past, when everybody carried a basket to the shops. Visitors came to see the famous plastic-free town, and soon many other towns in Britain wanted to do the same thing.

Today, many countries have laws about plastic bags. In England, big shops started charging money for them in 2015, and people now use far fewer bags. Of course, bags are only a small part of the problem of pollution. We also need to recycle bottles and stop dropping rubbish in the street. But Modbury shows that one small town, and one person, can do something big for the environment.
